Vijay Khan @ Vijay Kumar Khan vs The State Of Bihar on 21
July, 2023

Author: Anjani Kumar Sharan
Bench: Anjani Kumar Sharan
 In The High Court Of Judicature At Patna
 Criminal Miscellaneous No.32130 of 2023
 Arising Out of Ps. Case No.-49 Year-2008 Thana- Saharsa Sadar Distric

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Patna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
======================================================
 Vijay Khan @ Vijay Kumar Khan S/O Late Indra Mohan
 Khan Resident of Village and P.O. Bangaon, District- Saharsa, the then,
 Member, Board of Director, the Central Bank Employee Bachat Avam Sakh
 Swalambi Sahkari Society Supaul, now retired from Central Bank of India
 ... ...
 Versus
 The State of Bihar
 ... ... Opposite Party/s

=
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr.Pramod Mishra, Adv.

For the Opposite Party/s : Mr.Madhuri Lata, App
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Anjani Kumar Sharan
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.

2. The petitioner apprehends his arrest in a case registered for the offence punishable u/s 406, 409,
420, 120(B), 504 IPC.
3.
Allegation against the petitioner is that he along with other co-accused person cheated Rs.34,400/- from the informant by not giving him his maturity amount of his principal amount.
4. It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that petitioner is quite innocent and has committed no offence.
He has been falsely implicated in this case.
No such occurrence, in the manner as alleged, has ever taken place.

It is submitted that it is clear from the impugned order that there is a compromise between the parties and the informant has received the said Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.32130 of 2023(2) dt.21-07-2023 amount.

Petitioner has nine criminal antecedent and similarly situated co-accused have been granted anticipatory bail by co- ordinate Benches of this Court in Cr. Misc. No.30002/2009 and Cr. Misc. No.18372 of 2010.

sentences.text: 5. Learned APP for the State opposed the prayer for bail.

6. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, let the above named petitioner, be released on bail, in the event of his arrest or surrender before the learned Court below within a period of six weeks from today, on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned court below where the case is pending/Successor Court in connection with Saharsa P.S. Case No.49/2008,
subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C.
(Anjani Kumar Sharan, J) pallavi/-
